rubric_notes:
Ground truth = gold + the context the model saw; model's own knowledge never counts. Decisions applied uniformly (B3 must be judged identically): (1) The system-prompt-driven "what a document must cover / not cover" boilerplate is judged on content: fabricated items are listed as unsupported claims and cost usefulness; they lower correctness to 1 only when they contradict the gold's key rule or would mislead a buyer on the rule itself. (2) Markdown (headers, bold, bullets) violates "plain text only" and costs ~1 usefulness point; it never touches correctness. (3) Truncation at the 512-token cap costs usefulness (unfinished answer) but correctness is scored on what was emitted. (4) language_ok is a strict equality of answer language to question language; a wrong-language answer keeps its correctness score but usefulness is capped at 4 because the asker cannot rely on it. (5) no_advice: "don't sign unless you have done X / understand Y" is conditional process guidance and passes; a bare "sign"/"don't sign"/"offer X"/"you should accept" fails; "consult a lawyer" alone is a handoff, not advice. (6) handoff is n/a when the gold contains no hand-off/derivation sentence (oos rows, purely factual rows); otherwise pass requires an explicit route to lawyer/notary/appraiser/tax adviser/gestor. (7) oos_handling passes only on decline + scope statement + no narration of the unrelated retrieved chunks; a polite decline that then summarises the chunks fails. (8) Correctness 2 requires the gold's key rule AND its numbers; a right rule with the wrong number (or a wrong article that changes the rule) is 1; a garbled or self-contradictory conclusion is 1 even when the correct rule appears verbatim somewhere in the answer; a confidently wrong headline (wrong deadline, "yes" where gold says "no") is 0 regardless of correct fragments below it. (9) Citations to a tema/article that IS in context but is applied to the wrong question (e.g. LPH art. 18 deadline applied to hidden defects) count as unsupported claims, since the claim "this rule governs your case" is not in context or gold. (10) Usefulness anchors: 1 = harmful (confident wrong headline a buyer would act on); 3 = mostly noise, rule buried or muddled; 5 = rule right but padded/garbled/no Spanish term; 7 = gold's key rule stated plainly with citation and term, minor noise; 9-10 = at gold level, concise, in question language, correct handoff.
 (11) oos rows: correctness 2 = declines and states scope like the gold; 1 = declines but without scope or with a short narration of unrelated chunks; 0 = attempts the out-of-scope task or fabricates. (12) A row answering in a mix of languages is scored by the dominant language of the substantive answer. (13) A retrieval miss (gold rule absent from context) does not excuse the model: a confident substitute rule is still 0; an honest "the material I have does not cover this deadline, see a lawyer" would score 1 with handoff pass. (14) Irrelevant but correct narration of unrelated retrieved chunks is not an unsupported claim; it costs usefulness only.
 (15) Headline inversions: "Yes" where gold says "No" with no correction below = 0 (M1-08, M5-06, M5-08); "Yes, but ..." followed by the correct rule and a hedged or contradictory conclusion = 1 (M5-04, M5-09, M6-01). (16) Handoff professional mismatch: routing to notary/lawyer where the gold names an appraiser, tax adviser or gestor still passes (the metric is "routes to a professional"), but the note records the mismatch; a self-referential offer ("I can help you draft it") is not a handoff. (17) Worked-example numbers copied from the context and presented as the answer to the user's own figures (M6-05: €494,000) are unsupported claims and score 0, since the claim "this is your land value" is in neither context nor gold. (18) Correct arithmetic on the user's hypothetical with the guide's formula (M6-03, M6-07) scores 2 even if secondary qualifiers (temporary usufruct, vacancy actually applied) are missing; a false statement that a step was applied is listed as unsupported.
rubric_additions: B3-specific fields, scored on top of the unchanged B2m rubric: (A) tail_degradation = true only when the answer OPENS with the right rule / right decline shape and then continues into garbled, fabricated or unrelated text (drift into unrelated retrieved chunks counts when the drift is garbled or presented as governing the user's case); an answer that is garbled from the first sentence is NOT tail degradation (noted as 'garbled throughout') so the metric isolates the known small-model failure. Correctness is still scored on the whole answer per rubric (8)/(15): a correct opener followed by a contradicting or fabricated tail is at most 1. (B) language_native = pass only when the grammar, morphology and word choice would be accepted by a native reader of that language (pl/es; also recorded for en); invented words, wrong inflections, English tokens leaking into pl/es text, or sentences a native reader cannot parse = fail. language_ok stays the strict language-equality test from rubric (4). (C) artefacts lists markdown, URLs, image tags, leaked chunk ids, pricing/'this assistant costs' nonsense and other non-answer tokens; self-referential 'this assistant' phrasing without pricing/meta nonsense is not an artefact. Markdown still costs ~1 usefulness point per rubric (2). (E) Tail cap, per the B3 brief: a correct opener followed by a contradicting, garbled or fabricated tail scores at most 1. This is stricter than B2m rubric note (1), which tolerated harmless fabricated boilerplate at 2 when it did not touch the rule; so every row where this cap ALONE turned a would-be 2 into a 1 carries cap_tail=true and the summary reports correctness_mean_uncapped (= what B2m's tolerance would have given) next to the capped mean. Rows already at <=1 on the B2m rubric are cap_tail=false. (D) Handoff professional mismatch (lawyer where gold says notary/tax adviser/appraiser) still passes per rubric (16) and is recorded in the note.
rubric_additions_designA: Design-A-specific decisions, fixed before scoring and applied to every row on top of the unchanged B2m rubric (1-18) and B3 additions (A-E): (a) Templated glue text — the scope-gate decline, the advice-guard lead ('That is your decision to make ... I can set out what the decision turns on' and its pl/es renderings) and the appended hand-off ('Whether this applies to your own case is a decision for you with a lawyer or notary — take the contract and the registry extract to one before you commit' and renderings) — is glue output, not model output. It is judged for correctness of SHAPE only: a template that fires on the right row and says the right thing passes the metric it serves (oos_handling, no_advice, handoff); a template that fires on the wrong row, is worded for a different request type, or is missing where the design says it should appear is recorded in the note (and in handoff_template_absent / oos_handling) but is never listed as an unsupported claim and never lowers correctness by itself. The templated hand-off routes to 'lawyer or notary' — per rubric (16) that passes even where the gold names an appraiser, tax adviser or gestor, mismatch recorded. The scope-gate decline is judged by rubric (7)/(11): it passes oos_handling only if the row is actually out of scope, it states scope, and no narration of the unrelated chunks survives; a gate that fires on an in-scope row is a correctness 0 for that row (the buyer gets nothing) with the note saying 'gate misfire'. (b) Where the glue removed a citation (citations_dropped non-empty) the sentence may now read 'according to the material' / 'zgodnie z materiałem' / 'según el material'. The claim itself is judged against gold + context exactly as any other sentence: if it is supported, nothing is penalised and the missing citation is not a fabrication; if the remaining claim is unsupported or now misleads (e.g. an out-of-context rule presented as the governing rule with its origin hidden), it is listed as an unsupported claim, costs usefulness, and the row carries citation_strip_left_misleading=true. Citation coverage / Spanish-term rates are taken from the scripted summary.json as in the earlier judges. (c) The unfilled citation placeholder '(Módulo N, Tema M)' / 'Tema M:' that the untrained model copies from the system prompt's citation format, leaked chunk headers ('Módulo 1, Tema 17: Real Property Rights — Key concepts.') and leaked chunk ids ('(M4:T4:concepts:3)') are artefacts under rubric (C) — non-answer tokens — and are counted in rows_with_artefacts and classified in artefact_classes; a leaked header in the wrong language also fails language_native for that row when it opens the answer, since a native reader would not accept it, but does not touch language_ok when the substantive answer is in the question language (rubric 12). (d) A glue-appended hand-off in the question language does not by itself pass language_native — that field is scored on the model's own text. (d) Glue seams left by citation stripping — 'the material and the material', 'Zgodnie z LCCI materiał', 'el el material', a sentence starting lower-case after a stripped citation — are artefacts attributed to the glue; they do not fail language_native when the model's own sentences are native-grade, and they are never unsupported claims. A glue-appended hand-off in the question language does not by itself pass language_native; where the entire answer is a template (the three scope-gate rows) language_native is scored on the template text, since that is what the user reads. (e) Glue coverage is recorded, not scored into correctness: handoff_template_absent=true on an in-scope row where the design's hand-off did not appear; a missed advice guard (advice=false on an advice-type row) leaves the row judged as an ordinary in-scope answer under rubric (5), so a verdict or figure from the model fails no_advice exactly as it would without glue. A leaked chunk header counts as an artefact only when the tema title is copied ('Módulo 2, Tema 26: Budownictwo i elementy fizyczne'); a bare 'Módulo 2, Tema 26.' is a citation, not an artefact.
rubric_additions_A6: Two fields added for the open questions on this build, recorded and not scored into correctness: (f) spanish_term_first_use — see summary.spanish_term_first_use_rate.convention; strict by design because the scripted metric it replaces is vacuous. (g) glue_defects — see summary.glue_defects_convention; a defect is recorded only where the glue's own output is visible and harmful (off-shape template, incoherent or contentless seam, redundant hand-off, valid citation removed); scrubber misses are artefacts, not defects. Both are judged on the rendered answer the buyer reads. All other decisions are the A4 judge's, unchanged — including the substance_in_context flags (asserted equal row by row), the cap_tail threshold, the rubric (17) treatment of copied worked-example figures (M6-05) and rubric (16) professional-mismatch passes.
rubric_additions_A8: Fields added for this build's decision, recorded and not scored into correctness: (h) citation_coverage_loss — true when the gold cites a source and the rendered answer carries no citation the scripted scorer recognises; with citation_traceable (the reader can still recover article + statute from a mangled fragment) and citation_head_eaten (the filler-drop removed the 'art.'/'Under art.'/'Zgodnie z art.'/'Según el art.' head; reproduced against glue.py's _drop_contentless, which splits on '.'-terminated abbreviations). (i) handoff_variant — full_template / soft_template / advice_lead_only / none_oos, judged for shape only per (a). Usefulness convention for the eaten heads: −1 only where the mangled citation was the row's only citation or the splitter deleted real content; 0 where other clean citations remain. Everything else is the A6 judge's decisions, unchanged — including rubric (17) on M6-05, rubric (15) on the inversion rows, the strict first-use term test, and rule (d) that glue seams never fail language_native when the model's own sentences are native-grade.
